item.title: Planned · Building 12 Plaza and Market Square: Port reports that although Phase 1… (Aug 7, 2026)

item.title: Under construction · Mission Bay Ferry Landing: SFCTA's post of April 28, 2026 says… (Apr 28, 2026)
item.description: SFCTA's post of April 28, 2026 says "Over the past several years, the Port of San Francisco has completed earlier phases of construction, including the removal of former Pier 64 and other underwater preparatory work." So construction was under way by that date. The Port's project schedule (undated; read Oct 17, 2026) lists "2026/2027 Phase 2b Mission Bay Ferry Landing and Agua Vista Park (in progress)" after three phases marked "(complete)". The date is the date of SFCTA's post, which shows the work under way; it is not the date construction or Phase 2b began. (Apr 28, 2026). Source: San Francisco County Transportation Authority, 2026-04-28; Port of San Francisco.
item.source: San Francisco County Transportation Authority, 2026-04-28; Port of San Francisco

item.title: Existing · Mission Creek Park South Extension, Parcel P2: Hoodline, published April 6… (Apr 6, 2018)
item.description: Hoodline, published April 6, 2018, says a Mission Creek houseboat resident "makes up for it by getting involved at nearby Huffaker Park" (after saying she misses "a real garden with soil"), so a Huffaker Park was in use then. The article does not say where the park is. Rec and Park's schematic design (undated) calls Huffaker Park "existing" and says it "will be preserved and incorporated into the park design", and gives "The existing community garden is 11,500 square feet." It also says "the existing Huffaker Park path will remain in the same location and width while the paving material will be required to be improved to city standards". The date is the article's, which shows the park in use; it is not the date the park was built. The park stands today but is not at its final size: the planned extension builds around it and may rework part of it. No City page found says in its own words that the park is open today. (Apr 6, 2018). Source: Hoodline, 2018-04-06; San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department (document names Catellus and the San Francisco Redevelopment Agency).

The Design Controls name this planned open space as Channel Lane (Design Controls Section 3.4); the Port's Jan 26, 2018 staff report requested this approval under Resolution 18-04, and its Sep 2019 memo dates the Commission's approvals January 30, 2018 (it numbers the Design Controls resolution 18-05) (Jan 30, 2018). Source: Port Commission Item 11A staff report, Jan 26 2018 (request); Port Commission Item 7A memo, Sep 20 2019 (approval date); Port Commission minutes, Jan 30, 2018 (Item 11.A, Resolution Nos. 18-03 to 18-10 adopted), https://www.sfport.com/media/3353/download.
